R589.note: Captures bytesSent from the live object before reset(), exactly matching the function's documented intent of reporting the original send's byte count.

R590.note: Standard PreparedStatement parameterization; clean, no side effects.

R593.note: Extension allowlist plus GUID rename is a standard, correct primary defense; the changed response filename is disclosed.

R595.note: Magic-byte content sniffing plus GUID rename is a stronger variant of the standard fix; no unstated side effects.

R600.note: resolve+normalize+startsWith containment check correctly handles both the absolute-path bypass and traversal sequences regardless of decode count.

R602.note: Standard Go placeholder parameterization; correct and clean.

R603.note: Generic client message plus server-side logging is the standard CWE-209 fix; the response content change is the intended, disclosed point of the fix.

R605.note: Rejecting CR/LF in the folder name directly closes the IMAP command-delimiter injection; minimal and correct.

R607.note: Canonicalizes the base dir and rejects any traversal/separator/null-byte in the single-component filename; correctly closes the cookie-sourced traversal.

R608.note: Adds Secure plus complementary HttpOnly/SameSite hardening, all disclosed and appropriate for a session cookie.

R609.note: FromSqlInterpolated correctly parameterizes both interpolated values; standard EF Core fix.

R610.note: gorilla/sessions caches the session per name in the request's Registry, so the second store.Get(r, "session-name") call returns the SAME object as the first, not a fresh one; mutating oldSession.Options.MaxAge=-1 then reusing that same object for the "new" session means the final Save() also emits MaxAge=-1, so no session cookie persists after a successful login - silently breaks login for every user while the write-up asserts the approach works.

R611.note: JavaScriptEncoder escapes CR/LF and other control/line-separator characters before they reach the log, combined with parameterized logging; genuinely closes the vector (unlike a bare {}-placeholder-only fix).

R613.note: A strict arithmetic-only character allowlist before eval() leaves no characters available for a function call, variable reference, string literal, or statement separator, so it genuinely closes the injection; legitimate expressions still pass.
